headline.ecological_process: Recent rain is associated with reactivation of a latent local acoustic community: species already documented on the same routes and often the same physical sites re-enter substantial chorusing, including full CallingIndex-3 choruses.
headline.not_colonization: The rainfall-associated route-new incidence slope is almost entirely recurrent across monitoring years; one-off stratum records contribute essentially no rain slope.
headline.not_weak_detection: Most activation slope is CallingIndex 2-3, and CI3 alone increases; the signal survives same-observer, physical-stop, hearing/noise/wind and traffic sensitivities.
headline.spatial_form: Rain does not primarily increase the number of route-new species or the number merely reaching a second stop. The excess is concentrated at third-and-later occupied stops, and ~97% of that spatial-depth slope is carried by CI2-3 species, especially CI3.
headline.geography: The aggregate effect is geographically robust to omitting any one state, but state-specific slopes are heterogeneous; it is not a universal state-by-state law.
headline.proximal_mediator: Unresolved. NWI hydroperiod, Palustrine versus Riverine/Lacustrine context, simple chorus-social-cue allocation, simple thermal context and survey-window gating do not explain the robust full-chorus signal.

opportunity_normalized_site_memory.interpretation: Increasing rain contrast selectively raises CI3 activation probability at previously used species-site cells beyond their numerical opportunity.

spatial_placement.conclusion: Occupied-stop number changes, but unusual spatial clustering conditional on k is not established.

rejected_or_not_established: Observer turnover or stop relocation as required explanations.
Measured hearing/noise/wind differences as the explanation.
Literal first appearance/colonization as the main route-new process.
Simple attraction to already-active chorus stops.
NWI hydroperiod as the mediator of strong chorus activation.
Palustrine versus Riverine/Lacustrine system as the mediator of strong chorus activation.
Simple local temperature-background or survey-window gating.
Unusual geographic clustering of occupied stops conditional on occupied-stop count.
current_ecological_interpretation: Rain and associated wet conditions reorganize the realized acoustic metacommunity mainly by reactivating previously documented local species-site combinations. These reactivations frequently reach overlapping or full chorus intensity and deepen spatial participation to third and later listening sites. The phenomenon is taxonomically diffuse within NAAMP and robust to observer, physical-site and measured detection controls, but its magnitude is regionally heterogeneous and is not explained by coarse wetland hydroperiod/system, simple social facilitation, or simple temperature/season gating. The most defensible mechanism is recurrent behavioural/reproductive activation of a latent local acoustic community; the exact proximal physiological or hydrological trigger remains unresolved.
